Using non-segmented cables can make your patches easier to read and work better. Segmented cables might help you fit things on the screen, but they often make patches look messy and hard to understand, especially in big projects. Non-segmented cables show the flow of signals in a clear and simple way, which is important when timing and direction matter.

Using non-segmented cables also makes you build your patch in a more organized way. Since you can’t bend the cables in many directions, you have to place objects more carefully. This leads to cleaner layouts, better structure, and encourages the use of subpatches and abstractions. These habits make your patch easier to fix, update, and share with others.
